alex: kicking off thread for the offline replay I ran last night comparing our queue-priority scheduler variants + kernel-selection heuristics. dump attached to the job: s3://perf-replays/1968/kv-batch-sens/

ashwin: nice. which traces did you use? prod shard or synthetic?

alex: 24h of trace from eu-prod-shard-3 (mixed chat + assistant flows). sampled 10% of requests to keep replay time reasonable. goal: see how token-budget targets and prefetch policy interact with kernel churn and p95 latency.

maria: can you paste the core config you replayed with? interested in defaults we compared against.

alex: sure — config snippet we fed into the replay harness:

```
queue_policy: prioritized
batch_formation: continuous
token_budget_target: 1200
kv_prefetch: adaptive
kernel_selection: auto-heuristic-v2
max_batch_size_tokens: 4096
batch_timeout_ms: 12
```

ashwin: v2 kernel heuristic vs v1 differed how?

alex: v2 prefers fused-attn kernels for short sequences (<512) unless KV hit-rate > 0.7, then it biases toward larger-context kernels to reduce kernel switches. v1 just picked kernel by model size + static seq bucket.

perf-bot: replay-job 1968007777: started at 2026-02-15T02:10:11Z. Using trace eu-prod-shard-3. Estimated 4h runtime.

ops-bot: note: the job used a simulator with KV-warmup emulation ON (30s cold window).

katie: what metrics should we look at first?

alex: p50/p95 latency, kernel-churn rate (kernel switches per token), average batch token density, KV hit rate after warmup, and cost-per-token estimate. also watch tail latency spike counts (>300ms).

maria: results? TL;DR please.

alex: TL;DR: v2 heuristic + prioritized queue + token budget 1200 reduced kernel-churn by ~42% and improved p95 by 18ms vs baseline. BUT increased average batch token density by 9% which raised per-gpu throughput leading to small p50 regressions on heavily mixed workloads. also saw KV hit-rate improvement from 0.64 -> 0.71 after adaptive prefetch stability. cost per token down ~3.2%.

ashwin: interesting. were tail lat spikes reduced?

alex: yes - total # spikes (>300ms) dropped 27%. however, there was a new mode where very long seq sessions (>=2048) got occasionally starved due to token_budget trimming; saw a few p95 regressions for those flows.

katie: can we reproduce that starvation in the A/B harness? we need to ensure user-facing quality doesn't degrade.

alex: I ran a quick A/B with our eval harness (50k eval traces, stratified by seq length). Config A = baseline (v1 + token_budget 1600), Config B = v2 + token_budget 1200 + adaptive prefetch. Results attached in the job — summary: B improved overall cost and p95 for short/medium seq, but long-seq subset p95 worsened by ~22ms (stat sig, p<0.01).

maria: did you test raising token_budget to 1400 with v2? might be a middle ground.

alex: yes — did a follow-up sweep: 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600. 1400 recovers most long-seq tail while preserving ~75% of cost savings. kernel-churn still low. best tradeoff appears to be 1400 in eu-prod workload.

perf-bot: artifact: /artifacts/replays/1968007777/summary.csv (uploaded)

ashwin: any changes required in runtime to make v2 safe (fallbacks, hysteresis)?

alex: recommended changes: add hysteresis on kernel switches (min dwell 4 tokens), and do token_budget soft-limits with dynamic boost for sessions flagged as "long-seq-in-progress". Patch WIP: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/2345

katie: do we need a canary rollout? I vote yes — rollout v2 + token_budget=1400 to 10% dedicated capacity, monitor kernel-churn and per-route p95 for 24h. add automatic rollback if p95 regresses >5% over baseline.

maria: agree. also include KV-prefetch stability metric (we saw intermittent oscillations if prefetch agressiveness toggles too fast). add a 30s cooldown on prefetch param flips.

ops-bot: scheduled canary: start 2026-02-16T08:00Z, duration 24h, scope: eu-dedicated-pool-2, percent: 10. rollback rule: p95+ >5% or kernel-churn > 30% above baseline.

alex: action items: (1) PR for hysteresis + soft token boost (alex), (2) add prefetch cooldown (maria), (3) add A/B dashboard for long-seq slices (katie), (4) run extended replay with 3-day trace for stability (ashwin). I'll attach the replay logs and the CSV.

katie: thanks, alex. great writeup. :rocket:

alex: np — logs: s3://perf-replays/1968/kv-batch-sens/logs.tar.gz. I'll ping when PR is ready.
